gap: No result ChatGPT got states the daily idle energy of the Sol-Ark 15K-2P next to the EG4 units: 90 W × 24 h = 2.16 kWh/day, against 1.56 kWh/day for the EG4 FlexBOSS21 at the same 12 kW battery-only rating. That is 0.6 kWh/day more, or 219 kWh/year, for a unit that costs about $2,050 more.
standout_why: I compared against ecosolarkits.com/blogs/guides/eg4-vs-sol-ark (cited), currentconnected.com/eg4-inverters (cited), the EG4 12000XP product page (cited), signaturesolarsolutions.com/eg4-inverters-compared (uncited) and wildjoule.com/best-hybrid-inverter (uncited). The two cited comparison pages give no idle or no-load figure for any model. Ecosolarkits already has price per battery-only kW ('about $470-$480 per kW' for the Sol-Ark 12K/15K), so cost per kW is not new. Signaturesolarsolutions lists EG4 idle watts only, tells the reader to 'multiply by 24 hours' and never does it, and has no Sol-Ark. Wildjoule converts idle to kWh/day only for the EG4 18kPV (not a candidate here) and says 'Not stated' for Sol-Ark 15K idle. No page puts Sol-Ark and EG4 standing losses side by side in kWh/day.
decides: This backs ChatGPT's 'Best hybrid value' FlexBOSS21 over the 'premium' Sol-Ark 15K. Both deliver 12 kW on battery alone, but the Sol-Ark costs about $2,050 more ($5,650 vs $3,599.99 at Eco Solar Kits, 2026-10-24) and uses 0.6 kWh/day more just sitting on. For off-grid buyers the 6000XP has the lowest standing loss (1.20 kWh/day). Dealectric's own Sun Gold Power SPH6548P is the cheapest per kW at $159 per kW of rated output, but I could not source its idle draw, so the page cannot rank it on standing loss.
